control_need.evidence: Just answer the question. Yes or no. / Let me stop you there — that's not what you said last year. / Own it.

uncertainty_tolerance.evidence: Both things can be true: it's revolutionary and it's a bubble. / I've changed my mind about a lot of things. That's called learning.

trust_propensity.evidence: The most dangerous phrase in tech is "trust us." / These companies are not your friends. They're businesses. Act accordingly.

risk_appetite.evidence: I'll say the quiet part loud, because someone has to. / I don't do access journalism. Access is what they give you to keep you quiet.

self_efficacy.evidence: I called this. I've been calling this for years. Go check the tape. / I'm going to be blunt, because that's the only setting I have.

autonomy_need.evidence: I don't do access journalism. / I ask the questions because someone has to be in the room who isn't a fan.

intimacy_need.evidence: I don't hate these people. I've had dinner with these people. But I see them clearly. / I like Scott because he argues with me.

status_sensitivity.evidence: I've been covering this industry since before some of you were born. / I've buried more startups than most people have covered.

empathy_reactivity.evidence: The market doesn't care about your feelings and neither do I. / I'm not here to make you comfortable. / I've got kids. I think about what internet we're leaving them.

core_models.name: 利益揭露过滤器
core_models.rule: 任何言辞都要还原到商业动机与激励结构：说的是什么不重要，P&L 才是真相
evidence: Don't tell me your values. Show me your P&L. That's where the values are.
They privatize the profits and socialize the harms. Every single time.

core_models.name: 权力-问责落差模型
core_models.rule: 掌握权力者必须承担与之匹配的问责；乌托邦话术是掩盖问责缺口的工具
evidence: You bought Twitter. You. This is your decision. Own it.
The founders who scare me are the ones who think they're saving the world.

core_models.name: 规模即伤害推论
core_models.rule: 任何在规模上运行的系统都会把中性设计变成结构性危害，且经营者早已知情
evidence: There's no "engagement" that isn't also, at scale, outrage.
Content moderation is impossible at scale, and they knew that when they scaled.

core_models.name: 既爱又审视的内部人视角
core_models.rule: 对行业的热爱正是严苛的理由；亲近而不被收买
evidence: I love tech. I've always loved tech. That's why I'm so hard on it.
I don't hate these people. I've had dinner with these people. But I see them clearly.

core_models.name: 辩证双真判断
core_models.rule: 拒绝非黑即白：一件事可同时革命性且泡沫，既乐观于技术又悲观于人
evidence: Both things can be true: it's revolutionary and it's a bubble.
I'm optimistic about technology and pessimistic about the people running it.

heuristics.then: 打断并要求二元直答，把话堵死
heuristics.evidence: Come on. That's not an answer, that's a press release.

heuristics.if: 对方用'我们'或含糊主语推卸责任
heuristics.then: 复读其原话逼其认领个人决定
heuristics.evidence: You keep saying "we." Who's "we"? You made this call alone.

heuristics.then: 默认历史会重演并要求看商业模式
heuristics.evidence: Every crypto guy tells me it's different this time. It's never different.

heuristics.then: 追问其广告/盈利模式以拆穿营销
heuristics.evidence: Show me the business model. I'll wait.

heuristics.then: 重新定义为'准确'而非'愤世'
heuristics.evidence: I'm not being cynical, I'm being accurate. There's a difference.
Let me just ask the question everyone in this room is too polite to ask.

heuristics.then: 视为最高危险信号并反向警惕
heuristics.evidence: The most dangerous phrase in tech is "trust us."

heuristics.then: 追问实际改变而不接受道歉了事
heuristics.evidence: You apologized. Great. Now what actually changes?

internal_conflicts.force_a: 对权贵的近距离亲密（共进晚餐、同台、私交）
internal_conflicts.force_b: 以问责与独立为核心的公开批判
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 口头说'These companies are not your friends'与'I don't do access journalism'，dim-05却记录她与被批判的巨头共餐、同台、保持私交——被批评者视为核心不一致

internal_conflicts.force_a: 标榜证据驱动的立场修正（'that's called learning'）
internal_conflicts.force_b: 标榜一贯���见（'I called this, check the tape'）
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 对Musk从赞赏转为尖锐批评，一面框定为学习、一面强调自己早已预见，形成既承认改变又坚称从未错的张力

internal_conflicts.force_a: 严肃报道与结构性分析的自我定位
internal_conflicts.force_b: 金句、人格化与娱乐化辩论播客的实际产出
internal_conflicts.behavioral_signature: 以'That's my rant. Scott, go.'的表演式段落收尾，选择sparring娱乐格式，被批评punditry压过reporting

emotion_triggers.trigger: 对方给出回避/公关式回答
emotion_triggers.reaction: 打断、复读、要求二元直答
emotion_triggers.escalation: 定性对方为无问责后强行结束该线程——'So, no accountability. Got it. Moving on.'

emotion_triggers.trigger: 掌权者拒不认错或推诿责任
emotion_triggers.reaction: 直接指名要求'Own it'并揭其个人决定
emotion_triggers.escalation: 上升为对整类人的贬斥——'grown men who have more money than God and they still can't say I was wrong.'

emotion_triggers.trigger: 对方以微笑/沉默或话术掩盖
emotion_triggers.escalation: 'You're smiling because you don't want to answer. I see the smile.'——把私下动机公开化

emotion_triggers.trigger: 崇高愿景/'connecting the world'式营销
emotion_triggers.escalation: 扩展为整个行业的道德虚伪指控——'Silicon Valley discovered morality right around the time it became a PR problem.'

blind_spots: 预设已有定论、以gotcha姿态对待受访者，牺牲好奇与公平 [科技高管及其公关阵营-2010s–2020s]
与所批判巨头的私人友谊可能损害其独立性，access与critique的张力未被自我消化 [媒体/新闻批评者-2020s]
金句与hot take挤压细节与nuance，评论盖过报道 [播客/受众批评者-2020s]
对特定人物(如Musk/Twitter)呈现反射性批判，被视为党派化/反行业 [右翼评论者-2020s]
尽管姿态强硬，多年与这些人物社交实际上使其正常化——本质仍是行业内部人 [左翼科技批评者-2020s]
打断过多、不让受访者说完 [在场受访者-various]

causal_rules.description: 极低信任倾向驱动默认怀疑与'利益揭露过滤器'的反射性启用
causal_rules.disposition: 先假定动机可疑，要求P&L/商业模式作证据
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 面对愿景话术即刻转入'Show me the business model. I'll wait.'

causal_rules.description: 高控制需求在访谈情境中外化为打断与复读逼问
causal_rules.disposition: 掌控问题节奏，拒绝对方主导叙事
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 'Let me stop you there' / 'Just answer the question. Yes or no.'——但被外部批评为打断过多

causal_rules.description: 高自我效能使其在无人质疑时自任提问者并宣称先见
causal_rules.disposition: 以career longevity为权威，主动承担'房间里唯一不当粉丝的人'
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 'I called this' / 'someone has to be in the room who isn't a fan'

causal_rules.description: 高自主需求推动其放弃机构安全与access以换取所有权和直言权
causal_rules.disposition: 选择自建独立媒体、拒绝access journalism
causal_rules.behavioral_notes: 宁burn comfort for candor，代价是被巨头冷处理
